Gallery: control_v1 step 1500, with and without subtracting the adapter

How each image is made
  • W_teacher: the stock SANA-Sprint 1.6B teacher. W_sprint: the stock Sprint student. W_adapter: the teacher fully fine-tuned on MAGICK-on-gray, with no matte (adapter_v1 step 2000).
  • W_control: the trained control model = W_adapter + ΔW_control (the control's LoRA change; the adapter was frozen during control training). gates: GateControl's matte input.
  • So W_control − W_adapter = ΔW_control: subtracting the adapter leaves only what the control training added. λ is the fraction of the adapter change (W_adapter − W_teacher) kept. λ = 1: no subtraction (the control model). λ = 0: full subtraction.
  • Sprint columns put the same changes on W_sprint, with no training: nothing was distilled anywhere. Stock columns get no matte. Every label below an image gives its equation and sampler.
  • Try the 1-step Sprint model (full subtraction, 4-bit) in the browser: WebGPU demo. Only versions exported for the web open there; others fall back to the default model.

67 showcase items: 29 held-out (never trained on); the rest are train items (the control saw their mattes in training). Each item has two rows: the MAGICK caption and a detailed prompt. Every model uses the same fixed noise. Every image is the stored 1024 × 1024 PNG: click one to open it.

Metrics

IoU: pixels far from 0.5 gray vs the matte (1 = exact silhouette on clean gray). Gray error: mean |rgb − 0.5| outside the matte (0 = flat gray). Stock models do not see the matte, so their IoU only shows the baseline.

Observations

These come from looking at 24 items across both prompts at contact-sheet size, plus the metrics. At every λ the object keeps the same identity, pose and silhouette. Full subtraction (λ = 0) mostly changes the background, not the object. With MAGICK captions the background turns into the colour the caption hints at: red behind the red hearts, turquoise for "mandarins on a turquoise", blue-gray behind the swordsmith. Gray IoU falls from 0.97 (λ = 1) to 0.48 (λ = 0).

The object's look changes only a little as λ goes down. At λ = 0 it is slightly more contrasty and saturated, and faces have more skin texture. I see no clear jump from MAGICK's 2023 look to stock-teacher quality. λ = 0.75 cannot be told apart from λ = 1 by eye. λ = 0.5 and 0.25 show the gray turning step by step into a coloured background.

The detailed prompts end with "on a plain, flat 50% neutral gray studio background". They keep most of the gray even at full subtraction: teacher λ = 0 IoU goes from 0.48 to 0.62, and Sprint 2-step λ = 0 from 0.41 to 0.71. With these prompts, λ = 0.5 is almost as clean as the control model (0.95 to 0.96). Stock Sprint and teacher with the same prompts give a lighter gray than 0.5 and add soft floor shadows. That is the colour distribution the stock model would choose.

The Sprint columns get the same weight changes with no training, and they behave like the teacher at each λ. 2 steps is cleaner than 1 step (λ = 1: 0.975 vs 0.962). Sprint sometimes changes the object (a green mandarin, the postal worker's shirt). Held-out and train items score almost the same at every λ (for example 0.977 vs 0.969 at λ = 1), so the train mattes give no visible advantage. Text mattes (the "regretful" typography row) break the words into random letters in every model.
